---
title: "2. 2D Phase Portraits"
sidebar: usage
jupyter: python3
---

For 2D linear systems

$$
\dot{\vec x} = A\,\vec x, \qquad
A = \begin{pmatrix} a_{11} & a_{12} \\ a_{21} & a_{22} \end{pmatrix}
$$

the eigenvalues of $A$ classify the origin as node, focus, saddle, or center.
The legacy figure `PhasePortraitSaddle.png` shows the **saddle** case
$A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$
($\lambda_{\pm} = \pm\sqrt 2$).

We encode the system inline as a `Dynamics` and let
`plot_dynamics(..., kind="vectorfield")` draw the stream-plot.

```{python}
from tvbo import Dynamics
from tvbo.plot.dynamics import plot_dynamics
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

SADDLE_YAML = """
name: Saddle2D
description: |
  Two-dimensional linear ODE with saddle equilibrium at the origin.
state_variables:
  x1:
    name: x1
    domain: { lo: -2.0, hi: 2.0 }
    equation:
      lhs: Derivative(x1, t)
      rhs: x1 - x2
    initial_value: 0.5
  x2:
    name: x2
    domain: { lo: -2.0, hi: 2.0 }
    equation:
      lhs: Derivative(x2, t)
      rhs: -x1 - x2
    initial_value: 0.5
"""

dyn = Dynamics.from_string(SADDLE_YAML)
dyn.plot(kind='vectorfield')
```

The two real eigenvalues with opposite sign are visible as the orthogonal
stable / unstable manifolds crossing at the origin. Replacing the off-diagonal
entries with positive signs (or zeroing the diagonal) reproduces the other
canonical 2D phase portraits (node, focus, center) without changing any code
outside the YAML string.
